Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

position noun

a place, a location

also place, location, site, spot, in its place, scene (where something happens), the scene of the crime, the scene of the accident, on the scene, at the scene, on the spot, at your place, in place of, in the first place, this is not the place to

classical

Cato Agr. 68: in suō quidque locō repōnitō
Traupman 360

locus, locī m.

noun, second declension; plural locī (single spots, passages) and loca (places, a region)

place, position

suō quidque locō, each thing in its place.

Other words

  • situs, sitūs m. — situation, site (of a town, a house)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 2.22: urbis (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 7.36 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 206

    How a place lies; mostly of towns and land.

  • in rē praesentī — on the spot, at the scene itself

    also used · classical · Plaut. Cas. 2.8.65 (Lewis & Short, s.v. praesum); Cic. de Or. 1.250: in rem praesentem venīre (Lewis & Short)

    Of being at the place itself; to go to the place to see for oneself is in rem praesentem venīre (Lewis & Short, s.v. praesum).

Examples

  • omnia quīs ūsus erit, in suō quidque locō repōnitō

    put everything you will need back, each thing in its own placeCato Agr. 68

  • et castra eō ipsō locō ubi pugnātum erat, imperātor Rōmānus posuit.

    and the Roman commander pitched camp on the very spot where the battle had been fought.Liv. 34.26.3

  • apud tē

    at your placeTraupman 360

  • in locum parentis

    in place of a parentTraupman 360

  • prīmum

    in the first placeTraupman 360

  • Nōn est hic locus ut…

    This is not the place to…Traupman 360

See also position, put, here, scene, scene.
